_citation: Grav, T., Bauer, J. M., Mainzer, A. K., Masiero, J. R., Nugent, C. R., Cutri, R. M., Sonnett, S. & Kramer, E. (2015), 'NEOWISE: observations of the irregular satellites of Jupiter and Saturn', Astrophysical Journal 809, 3. DOI:10.1088/0004-637X/809/1/3. Text source: arXiv:1505.07820v1.
_transcription: Table 1 (p. 4): absolute magnitude H (V band, 1 AU from Sun and observer, zero phase, IAU H-G system) and slope parameter G as collected by the authors from Luu (1991), Rettig et al. (2001), Grav et al. (2003), Grav & Bauer (2007) and Bauer et al. (2006). Caption: 'for all the Jovian irregular satellites observed here, the absolute magnitude is found using an assumed value of IAU phase slope parameter G = 0.10 +- 0.15'. Table 3 (p. 7): NEOWISE thermal-model diameter and visible geometric albedo (for Phoebe the first of the two tabulated fits, the one discussed in Sec. 4.12). Only satellites with pck00011 radii are transcribed.
earth_phase_limit_note: Largest phase angles at which Jupiter's and Saturn's satellites are seen from Earth (the H, G fits rest on such data); the tabulated NEOWISE observations were at 11.2-12.2 deg (Jupiter) and 6.0-6.2 deg (Saturn), Table 1.
